teaching_method_trix.title: T.R.I.X Teaching Method
teaching_method_trix.description: Four foundational pillars to use when teaching every skill or physical preparation.

pillars.name: Tell / Show
points: Tell the student what you're expecting
Check student's understanding by asking questions before you start
Ensure your instructions are clear and precise
Show or demonstrate to the student the final version of what you're about to teach

pillars.name: Re-shape
points: Talk through the shapes necessary for the skill/activity
Beware of common misconceptions of shaping students may have for skills
Physically take student through stages of the skill, shape by shape
Analyse the student's shape by recording/taking photos at the start, middle and end of the skill

pillars.name: In support
points: Where possible, you must physically hand-support (spot) student when undertaking new skills
Communicate to the student which parts of the body you will support
Take the student through the skill slowly before supporting at full speed
Complete in-person risk assessment before supporting (risk to yourself & student)

pillars.name: Xaggerate (teaching points)
points: Have your key teaching points ready and communicate this with student
After each iteration/attempt, pick maximum 2 key teaching points to give feedback
Don't be afraid to reiterate the same teaching point in a different way
Exaggerate your teaching point by doubling up on teaching methods

pillars.name: Trust
points: Students must be able to trust you from the first time you interact with them
Parents must be able to trust you from the very first time you speak with them
Other teachers must be able to trust you
You must put your trust in students, teachers and parents alike
Don't say, do or make any decisions which could deem you or your actions as untrustworthy
Be 100% confident in your teaching so you give reason for others to trust you more

pillars.name: Engagement
points: If the student isn't engaged, the student will not progress
Use humour as much as possible to keep students engaged
Use different inflective tones of voice to engage whilst teaching
Constantly ask students questions, and quiz them on their own training
Research new ways to teach/spot current skills; keep the planning process engaging with new suggestions

pillars.name: Authority
points: It is important to have the respect of students in any given class
You are an authority in the class, and whilst the main teacher has authority over you, you have authority too
Remember you must try to maintain good rapport with students, but do not try to act as a best friend
Your decision making must reflect the fact you are in a position of authority with a level of responsibility
Use disciplinary procedures as outlined by your school or gym in order to maintain authority where necessary

pillars.name: Care (duty of)
points: You absolutely have a duty of care, and must follow your safeguarding policy at all times
You are acting 'in loco parentis' as well as the teachers you teach with
Ensure you have an up to date Safeguarding & Protecting Children certificate whilst teaching U18s
Understand that you are a role model and students will often copy your behaviour
Be aware of the common types of abuse, common signs for them, and what you should do if you see any

pillars.name: Humility
points: Show humility and don't act like you have all the answers to everything - you don't!
Be as student-centred as possible. It is not about you, it is all about the student
Practice patience alongside being humble. Understand students progress at different speeds
Change your teaching style to suit individual students and different age ranges
Seek advice and learn from your Principal/Head Coach: always seek to expand your knowledge

categories.name: Body Part Placement
categories.description: The understanding of where different body parts need to be to effectively perform a skill, at all stages throughout.

categories.name: Weight Distribution
categories.description: Knowing directional motion of the body during a skill: leaning, turning, twisting.

categories.name: Applied Force & Speed
categories.description: Ensuring the correct force (push or pull) is being implemented with the necessary amount of speed and/or energy.

types.name: Active Stretching
types.description: No external force is provided. You are actively moving one muscle group to stretch another. Can be completed without a stretching partner or accessories.

types.name: Passive Stretching
types.description: An external force is provided. You are being stretched instead of actively stretching - via partner stretches, accessories, or gravity.

types.name: Dynamic Stretching
types.description: Similar to active stretching (no external force), but performed with fast movement (e.g. kicks).

acrotrix_tips: Passive static stretches are great for improving flexibility but should only be implemented AFTER a good warm up / pulse raiser
Active stretches should be used directly after passive stretches, and can be used to determine progressions in flexibility
Dynamic stretches are great for improving moving flexibility (e.g. leaps) and promote blood flow to the exercised muscle groups prior to skills work

practical_exam_guidance.aim: Cover the allocated two practical skills in a video recording of 20-30 mins in length, live or an online session with ideally two students.
dos: Have ideally two students to work with
Record a max 30-min video, warm up carried out BEFORE filming - up to 15 mins per skill
Adhere to current government guidelines specific to your location
Read through logbook notes and prepare ahead of the recording
Plan how you will break down the skill set
Contact ACROTRIX for a refresher class if needed
Ensure a clear, spacious area with good visibility and audio
Review the video and submit via an UNLISTED YOUTUBE LINK
donts: Don't send a video of only 5-10 mins or only the final skill
Don't film just yourself - show everyone and how you are supporting
Don't book a hall/students until you've been given the two skills to teach
Don't send the video until reviewed, backed up, and requirements checked
Don't give up - 1:1s, refreshers and catch-ups are available
points_to_consider: Engage with your students, ask them if they know how to do a skill
Ask similar questions in different ways to allow a different perspective
Acknowledge risk and how to mitigate it
Correct via the three learning styles: Auditory, Kinaesthetic, Visual
Give a summary of feedback after a completed skill
